precepts.text: One: at the Red Sea. Because there were no graves in Egypt, hast thou taken us away to die in the wilderness? It had been better for us to serve the Egyptians.
precepts.point: Because all those men which have seen my glory and my miracles have tempted me now these ten times, and have not hearkened to my voice. Write the ten down; the Most High deals in numbers, and nothing in the Bible is insignificant.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Numbers 14:22 says they “have tempted me now these ten times, and have not hearkened to my voice”. These ten times are the countless acts of stubbornness of the children of Israel, and that is why the Lord asked “How long will this people provoke me?” Write them down. The Most High deals in numbers, and nothing in the Bible is insignificant.

Number one is at the Red Sea. “And they said unto Moses, Because there were no graves in Egypt, hast thou taken us away to die in the wilderness? wherefore hast thou dealt thus with us, to carry us forth out of Egypt? Is not this the word that we did tell thee in Egypt, saying, Let us alone, that we may serve the Egyptians? For it had been better for us to serve the Egyptians, than that we should die in the wilderness.”

They were complaining to Moses. The Lord had just brought them out with his glory and his miracles, and the first thing they did at the sea was wish themselves back in Egypt serving the Egyptians.

precepts.text: All our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea. Paul is speaking to the Corinthians: if they all passed through the sea, that means the Corinthians were Israel, because no Egyptians passed through the sea. And the mixed multitude that came out died in the wilderness. Baptized unto Moses means Moses taught us God's laws. They drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ. Who was following us in the wilderness? Christ. Who killed the Egyptians? Christ.
precepts.point: The waters returned and covered the chariots and the horsemen: there remained not so much as one of them. Thus the Lord saved Israel that day out of the hand of the Egyptians, and Israel saw the Egyptians dead upon the sea shore. And the people feared the Lord, and believed the Lord, and his servant Moses. We celebrated Passover.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

precepts.why:
Exodus 14 is one of the wars of the Lord: the Lord fought for Israel, overthrew the Egyptians in the midst of the sea, and “there remained not so much as one of them.” Paul looks back on the same crossing: “Moreover, brethren, I would not that ye should be ignorant, how that all our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea”.

That cloud is a chariot. And who is Paul speaking to? The Corinthians. If all their fathers passed through the sea, then the Corinthians were Israel. Did the Egyptians pass through the sea? No. And some will say there was a mixed multitude; the mixed multitude came out lusting after evil things and all died in the wilderness. If the wicked of our own people did not make it, what about the mixed multitude?

“And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea”: baptized unto Moses means Moses taught us; he taught us God's laws. “And did all eat the same spiritual meat; And did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.”

Who was following us in the wilderness? Christ. Who killed the Egyptians? Christ. The Lord who fought for Israel at the Red Sea, the one Moses wrote of, was always Christ, and he is the one who will come back and smite spiritual Egypt, the land we live in today.

precepts.text: The Lord went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, and by night in a pillar of fire. That pillar of cloud is a chariot, and the Lord was inside it: that is the Rock that followed them. He took not away the pillar of the cloud by day, nor the pillar of fire by night.
precepts.point: The waters returned and covered the chariots and the horsemen: there remained not so much as one of them. Thus the Lord saved Israel that day out of the hand of the Egyptians, and Israel saw the Egyptians dead upon the sea shore. And the people feared the Lord, and believed the Lord, and his servant Moses. We celebrated Passover.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

precepts.why:
In Exodus 14:19-20 “the pillar of the cloud went from before their face, and stood behind them: And it came between the camp of the Egyptians and the camp of Israel; and it was a cloud and darkness to them, but it gave light by night to these”. Who was in that pillar? Exodus 13:21 says it: “And the Lord went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, to lead them the way; and by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light; to go by day and night”.

Who went before them in the pillar of cloud? Christ. That pillar of cloud is a chariot, and the Lord was inside it. It is the Rock that followed them in 1 Corinthians 10. Imagine seeing something bright, what you would call a UFO today, come down and stand between you and your enemy. The Egyptians saw that, and you know they were afraid.

“He took not away the pillar of the cloud by day, nor the pillar of fire by night, from before the people.” Day and night it was with them. And it was through that same “pillar of fire and of the cloud” that the Lord looked unto the host of the Egyptians in the morning watch, troubled them and took off their chariot wheels, until they said “Let us flee from the face of Israel; for the Lord fighteth for them against the Egyptians.”

precepts.text: Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of the Lord: for the Egyptians whom ye have seen to day, ye shall see them again no more for ever. The scripture already said we would never see those Egyptians again; so the Egypt of Deuteronomy 28:68 cannot be ancient Egypt.
precepts.point: The definition of Egypt, from the Hebrew Mizraim, was read in class: shut in, restraint, misery, tribulation, distress. So when Moses says you will go into Egypt again with ships, it means we would go into a place of captivity, misery, and tribulation, and we would be carried there on ships.

note.label: Passover Class: Exodus From America Modern Day Egypt

precepts.why:
Deuteronomy 28:68 says “the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships, by the way whereof I spake unto thee, Thou shalt see it no more again”. Moses is being very specific, and Exodus 14:13 explains it. At the Red Sea he told the people: “Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of the Lord, which he will shew to you to day: for the Egyptians whom ye have seen to day, ye shall see them again no more for ever.”

The scripture already said we would never see those Egyptians again, for ever. So when Moses says we will go into Egypt a second time, the Egypt he is speaking of cannot be ancient Egypt. The people would have said, Egypt again? We are going back to Egypt a second time? And he explains: I am not talking about the Egypt you just came out of. The way whereof I speak unto thee, thou shalt see it no more again. It is a different Egypt.

And this time we go into it with ships. Moses saw the end. The Lord showed him the Israelites thrown on cargo slave ships and brought here to America: the transatlantic slave trade. Egypt, from the Hebrew Mizraim, means shut in, restraint, misery, tribulation, distress. So going into Egypt again means going into captivity, misery and tribulation again, carried there on ships, sold to our enemies for bondmen and bondwomen. That is why Revelation 11:8 calls the great city, Mystery Babylon, America, spiritually Egypt.

precepts.text: A very froward generation, children in whom is no faith; that is the record over Israel.
precepts.point: In captivity the people wax old in mind and will not depart: woe to the bloody city, the prey departed not. Israel was the prey in Egypt and did not want to leave, the same as now.

note.label: Exodus 14: The Salvation of the Lord at the Red Sea

precepts.why:
The Lord had done miracle after miracle before their eyes and brought them out with an high hand, yet at the first sight of the Egyptians marching “they were sore afraid”, and said he had taken them away “to die in the wilderness”. At the first sign of danger Israel lost all faith.

That is the record over Israel: “I will hide my face from them, I will see what their end shall be: for they are a very froward generation, children in whom is no faith.” Our people have always been a rebellious people of little faith, a very froward generation, children in whom is no faith. What they said at the sea is what the Lord said of them.

precepts.text: If we let him thus alone the Romans shall come; the same spirit feared the oppressor more than the Most High.
precepts.point: In captivity the people wax old in mind and will not depart: woe to the bloody city, the prey departed not. Israel was the prey in Egypt and did not want to leave, the same as now.

note.label: Exodus 14: The Salvation of the Lord at the Red Sea

precepts.why:
“Let us alone, that we may serve the Egyptians”; “it had been better for us to serve the Egyptians, than that we should die in the wilderness.” Serving the slave master felt easier than having faith in the Most High, and the same spirit was in Israel in the days of Christ.

“Then gathered the chief priests and the Pharisees a council, and said, What do we? for this man doeth many miracles. If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him: and the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation.” They confessed he did many miracles, and still their fear was the Romans. The fear of the oppressor outweighed belief in the miracles, the same as at the sea, where the Egyptians marching outweighed everything the Lord had done in Egypt.

That is the same word our people speak today: why are you stirring up trouble, why tell us to come out of the ways of Babylon; let us alone to serve the slave master.

precepts.text: The prey departed not; in captivity the people wax old in mind and will not leave.
precepts.point: In captivity the people wax old in mind and will not depart: woe to the bloody city, the prey departed not. Israel was the prey in Egypt and did not want to leave, the same as now.

note.label: Exodus 14: The Salvation of the Lord at the Red Sea

precepts.why:
“Woe to the bloody city! it is all full of lies and robbery; the prey departeth not”. In captivity the people wax old in mind and will not depart. Israel was the prey in Egypt, and the prey did not want to leave: “Let us alone, that we may serve the Egyptians”. Even out of Egypt, at the first sight of Pharaoh they wanted back.

It is the same now. The people sit in a bloody city full of lies and robbery, and the prey departeth not; they say let us alone to serve the slave master, because serving him feels easier than having faith in the Most High.

precepts.text: The salvation of the righteous and the destruction of the enemies were accepted together; the Lord glorified Israel by punishing the adversary.
precepts.point: Even the ground testified: where water stood before, dry land appeared, and a green field came up out of the violent stream; grass sprang up at the bottom of the sea for the people to pass.

note.label: Exodus 14: The Salvation of the Lord at the Red Sea

precepts.why:
“Israel saw the Egyptians dead upon the sea shore.” Their salvation was Egypt's destruction, in the same hour: the Red Sea opened for Israel and closed on Egypt. We have to accept that.

The Wisdom of Solomon says it plainly. “Of that night were our fathers certified afore, that assuredly knowing unto what oaths they had given credence, they might afterwards be of good cheer. So of thy people was accepted both the salvation of the righteous, and destruction of the enemies. For wherewith thou didst punish our adversaries, by the same thou didst glorify us, whom thou hadst called.” The salvation of the righteous and the destruction of the enemies were accepted together; the very thing that punished the adversary is what glorified Israel.

Whoever hates that the Most High saves one nation by destroying the others will have to come to grips with it. The people saw that great work, and “feared the Lord, and believed the Lord, and his servant Moses.” The Lord who brought us out the first time with great signs and wonders will save Israel out of this captivity the same way, and that is why the brothers and sisters must have faith in these last days: a trial is the true test of faith.

precepts.text: Creation itself was fashioned anew to keep the children without hurt; a green field out of the violent stream, and afterward the quails, which come later in the wilderness.
precepts.point: Even the ground testified: where water stood before, dry land appeared, and a green field came up out of the violent stream; grass sprang up at the bottom of the sea for the people to pass.

note.label: Exodus 14: The Salvation of the Lord at the Red Sea

precepts.why:
“the children of Israel walked upon dry land in the midst of the sea; and the waters were a wall unto them on their right hand, and on their left.” Even the ground testified. “For the whole creature in his proper kind was fashioned again anew, serving the peculiar commandments that were given unto them, that thy children might be kept without hurt: As namely, a cloud shadowing the camp; and where water stood before, dry land appeared; and out of the Red sea a way without impediment; and out of the violent stream a green field”.

Creation itself was fashioned anew to keep the children without hurt. Where water stood before, dry land appeared, and a green field came up out of the violent stream: grass sprang up at the bottom of the sea for the people to pass. “Wherethrough all the people went that were defended with thy hand, seeing thy marvellous strange wonders. For they went at large like horses, and leaped like lambs, praising thee, O Lord, who hadst delivered them.”

They were still mindful of what was done in Egypt, “how the ground brought forth flies instead of cattle, and how the river cast up a multitude of frogs instead of fishes.” And afterward, when “being led with their appetite, they asked delicate meats”, “quails came up unto them from the sea for their contentment”; that comes later in the wilderness. The Lord who fashioned creation anew for Israel at the sea will save Israel out of this captivity the same way, and that is why the brothers and sisters must have faith in these last days.

precepts.text: The Egyptians pursued into the midst of the sea; the Lord took off their chariot wheels, the sea returned to his strength, and there remained not so much as one of them.
precepts.point: This is part of the history Moses was recounting: remember what the Lord did for your fathers.

note.label: Deuteronomy 11: Remember His Acts, Keep His Commandments

precepts.why:
Here is the history Moses recounts, to the generation whose own eyes saw it. “And the Egyptians pursued, and went in after them to the midst of the sea, even all Pharaoh’s horses, his chariots, and his horsemen.” In the morning watch the Lord looked unto the host of the Egyptians through the pillar of fire and of the cloud and troubled them, “And took off their chariot wheels, that they drave them heavily: so that the Egyptians said, Let us flee from the face of Israel; for the Lord fighteth for them against the Egyptians.”

Then the Lord told Moses to stretch out his hand over the sea, “and the sea returned to his strength when the morning appeared; and the Egyptians fled against it; and the Lord overthrew the Egyptians in the midst of the sea. And the waters returned, and covered the chariots, and the horsemen, and all the host of Pharaoh that came into the sea after them; there remained not so much as one of them.”

That is “what he did unto the army of Egypt, unto their horses, and to their chariots; how he made the water of the Red sea to overflow them as they pursued after you”. Remember what the Lord did for your fathers: he took the wheels off their chariots, brought the sea back on them, and destroyed them unto this day.
